title: Debt Snowball vs Avalanche: Which Actually Wins? (Real Numbers)

lines.say: Debt snowball, or debt avalanche? People argue about this constantly.
So let's just run the numbers, and see which one actually wins.
Here's our example. Three debts.
A credit card, thirty-two hundred dollars at twenty-four percent.
A personal loan, eight hundred at twelve percent.
And a car loan, nine thousand at seven percent.

scene.label: Minimums add up to $376
scene.sub: a month goes to debt, every month

lines.cap: The minimums add up to $376. We'll put $900 a month toward debt.
lines.say: The minimums add up to three seventy-six. We'll put nine hundred a month toward debt, every month.
Both methods pay every minimum. The only question is where the extra goes.
First, the avalanche. Extra money goes to the highest interest rate first.
So the credit card is first.
Then the personal loan, then the car.

scene.head: Avalanche: month each debt is gone

lines.say: The credit card is gone in month six.
The personal loan, month seven.
And the car loan, month sixteen. Debt-free.
Now the snowball. Extra money goes to the smallest balance first, no matter the rate.

scene.head: Snowball: month each debt is gone

lines.say: The personal loan is gone in month two.
The credit card, month seven.
And the car loan, month sixteen. The same finish line.
So, which one wins?
The avalanche costs eight hundred and five dollars in interest.
The snowball costs eight forty-seven.
The difference is forty-two dollars. Over sixteen months.

scene.head: Your first debt is gone in…

lines.say: But look at this. With the avalanche, your first win comes in month six.
With the snowball, it's month two.

scene.text: The best method is the one you don't quit.

lines.say: And the best method is the one you don't quit.
If you need quick wins to stay motivated, the snowball's extra cost is small. If you're steady and want the least interest, go avalanche.

scene.label: What really made the difference
scene.sub: a month, every month. Minimums only would take 4½ years and $3,393 in interest.

lines.cap: The real win was the $900 a month. Minimums only: about 4½ years and $3,393 in interest.
lines.say: And remember, the real win here was the nine hundred dollars a month. Paying only the minimums would take about four and a half years, and cost over three thousand dollars in interest.
